1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3.strategy: The flexible developing move: the knight watches e4 and d5, and White can still choose between a broad pawn centre and a quieter set-up. Black gets to pick the first central break and the pawn structure that goes with it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4.strategy: Claims the whole centre at once, with pawns on c4, d4 and e4. Black must now undermine it from a distance, and White has to keep the big centre supported; the reward is space and the initiative, the risk is a centre that becomes a target.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3.strategy: Develops the king's knight and keeps the pawn centre in reserve: White can still choose between building it with e4 and a quieter set-up. The price is that Black gets the first say in the centre, and an early strike there meets a White position that has committed little.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6.strategy: Covers e5 and c5 and keeps the structure compact. Black has no weakness, prepares to develop the king's knight and castle, and waits to strike at the big white centre with flank pawn breaks. White has the space, Black the solid position.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5.strategy: Attacks d4 at once with a pawn, backed by the bishop on g7, so White must settle the centre now. Black gets quick counterplay without waiting for development; the cost is an early commitment that can lead to sharp play with the queen out early.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5.strategy: Strikes at the centre at once, but White simply takes with cxd5, and recapturing with the queen loses it to exd5. After ...c6 White keeps the extra pawn, and Black has little to show for it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 e5.name: Modern Defence: Neo-Modern Defence
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 e5.strategy: Challenges the centre head-on, but White simply takes: the g7 bishop recaptures into the open, and Nf3 hits it with tempo. Black stays solid, but White develops with gain of time and the bishop has to move again.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5.strategy: Takes space and closes the centre, giving White a lasting grip on the queenside. It also opens the long diagonal for the g7 bishop, aimed at b2 and at the c3 square, so White must watch that diagonal. A game of space against counterplay.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops and defends d4 a second time, so the pressure from the c-pawn and the bishop can be met calmly. If Black captures on d4, White recaptures with the knight and clamps down on d5 with pawns on c4 and e4.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nc3.strategy: Develops and guards e4, but leaves d4 short of defenders: after ...cxd4 the knight cannot recapture, and Qxd4 runs into ...Bxd4. White is a pawn down for only a little activity.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 d6.strategy: Defends the c5 pawn and covers e5, reaching a compact structure with an open diagonal for the g7 bishop. White has more space, but Black has no weakness and plays for queenside pawn breaks and pressure on the long diagonal.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 Qa5+.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Benoni Pterodactyl
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 Qa5+.strategy: Checks and guards c5, but Bd2 hits the queen at once, so it must move again while White develops with tempo. White keeps the space on d5, and Black has spent time for nothing.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 Nf6.strategy: Develops with an attack on e4, which nothing defends yet, so White must spend a move on it. Black keeps the structure flexible and prepares to castle; White's space on d5 and e4 stays, but those pawns now have to be defended rather than just held.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 d6 5.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight and guards e4, so the space advantage is supported. The bishop on g7 attacks the knight, which is guarded by the b2 pawn, and White has to watch that diagonal while Black plays for queenside breaks.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 d6 5.Nf3.strategy: Develops the king's knight toward castling and covers e5 and d4, so the space gained by the pawns on c4, d5 and e4 is held by pieces as well. The c3 square stays free for the other knight; Black's plan is queenside pawn breaks, and White has to be ready for them.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.d5 d6 5.Be2.strategy: A solid, slightly passive set-up: the bishop prepares castling behind the pawn chain and the space on c4, d5 and e4 is kept. It does nothing against Black's queenside pawn breaks or the pressure of the g7 bishop, so Black can organise its play without hurry.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nc3 d6.strategy: Defends c5 and covers e5, but passes up a free pawn: d4 is attacked by the c-pawn and the g7 bishop and defended only by the queen. Black stays solid, yet White gets time to support the centre and stands a shade better.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nc3 cxd4.strategy: Wins a pawn that White cannot hold: d4 is attacked by the c-pawn and the g7 bishop and defended only by the queen, and recapturing with the queen loses it to ...Bxd4. Even when the knight attacks d4 again, Black can guard it and keep the extra pawn; White has little to show for it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nc3 Bxd4.strategy: Takes the pawn with the bishop, which is safe on d4: if the queen takes it, the c5 pawn takes the queen. The bishop eyes b2 and f2, and Black keeps the extra pawn; the cost is that White gains time by chasing the bishop with the knight.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6.strategy: The sober move: supports c5 and e5 and keeps the queen at home. Black reaches a compact structure and lets the pressure on d4 from the c-pawn and the bishop do the work, while White's space has no target yet.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qb6.name: Modern Defence: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Polish Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qb6.strategy: Attacks the b2 pawn, which the c1 bishop guards, and defends c5, adding pressure on White's queenside. An early queen outing, however, can become a target while White develops with tempo.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+.name: Modern Defence: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Pterodactyl Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+.strategy: The check guards c5, but White answers with a developing move, so Black gains little for the early queen sortie. The queen on a5 stays exposed to harassment.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.Be2.strategy: Develops the bishop and prepares to castle; d4 is still guarded twice, so the centre holds. White keeps the space advantage and lets Black declare its intentions. Solid rather than ambitious.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.dxc5.strategy: Opens the centre and the long diagonal for the g7 bishop. After Black's natural recapture White can trade queens with check, which costs Black the right to castle; White gives up the space advantage for a simpler game in which Black's displaced king is the problem.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight and guards e4 and d5, so the centre is held by pieces as well as pawns. The knight can be pinned against the king by a queen on a5, and d4 is attacked twice, so White has to recapture there with a piece.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.d5.strategy: Closes the centre and gains space, ending the tension on d4. The pawn on d5 cramps Black's pieces, but it also opens the long diagonal of the g7 bishop toward b2, so White will want Nc3 to block it, and Black gets a clear plan of queenside pawn breaks.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.Be2.name: Modern Defence: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Pterodactyl Variation Declined
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.Be2.strategy: The queen check that gives the line its character: the queen leaves the d-file with tempo and aims down the diagonal at e1. A knight that blocks on c3 is pinned and cannot recapture on e4, so White must untangle at some cost, while Black's queen is out early and can be chased.

The natural developing move: the knight attacks e4, which nothing defends yet, and Black prepares to castle. It commits to nothing in the centre, so Black can still decide whether and when to exchange on d4; White has the space but must defend it.

Trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn and opens the diagonal of the g7 bishop. After the knight recaptures, the pawns on c4 and e4 give White a firm grip on d5 and b5, so Black plays against that bind with piece pressure and a later pawn break.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.dxc5.name: Modern Defence: Semi-Averbakh Variation, Pterodactyl Variation Accepted
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 d6 5.dxc5.strategy: Wins the pawn back with tempo: the check also hits c5, which nothing of White's guards. White has to answer the check, and Black recovers the material with a queen on an active square and no structural damage.

Recaptures the pawn at once, but White can trade queens with check: Black has to recapture with the king and can no longer castle. Black's active pieces should hold the balance, yet it is Black who has to prove it.

Develops with an attack on e4 and delays the recapture on c5. White defends with a developing move, and Black takes the pawn back later, when White can trade queens and cost Black castling. Sound, but a touch slower than recapturing at once.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+ 5.Nc.strategy: Blocks the check with a developing move that also guards e4. The cost is that the knight is pinned against the king by the queen and cannot move until White unpins it. White keeps the big centre, Black keeps the early activity.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+ 5.Bd.strategy: Blocks the check with the bishop, so both knights stay free to develop, and invites a queen exchange that suits the side with more space. The cost is time: if Black declines and goes after b2, White has to spend a move covering the pawn.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+ 5.Nb.strategy: Blocks with the queen's knight, which shuts the queen out of the defence of d4. After ...cxd4 the knight on f3 cannot recapture without losing a piece to ...Bxd4, so White simply loses a pawn.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+ 5.Nc.name: Pterodactyl Defence
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 c5 4.Nf3 Qa5+ 5.Nc.strategy: Supports the c5 pawn and frees the bishop on c8. Black keeps the pin on c3 and the pressure on d4, where the c-pawn and the bishop on g7 face White's queen and knight, and builds a sturdy base for the fight against White's big centre.

Develops with an attack on e4: the pinned knight on c3 cannot capture there, so White has to defend the pawn with a piece or break the pin at once. Black gains a tempo, keeps the pressure on c3 and d4 and prepares to castle.

Trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn and opens the long diagonal for the g7 bishop, while the pin on c3 stays. The pawns on c4 and e4 keep d5 and b5 out of Black's reach, so the play comes from piece activity against the centre.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5.strategy: Wins a pawn and keeps the pawns on c4 and d4, but ...c6 at once opens lines against White's centre. After dxc6 Bxd4 the extra pawn is worth little against Black's active pieces, and the game is close to level, so much of White's advantage is gone.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.cxd5.strategy: Takes with the c-pawn and wins a pawn, leaving pawns on d4, d5 and e4: a broad centre that cramps Black. The doubled d-pawns are the price, and Black's play comes from hitting the front pawn with pieces and a pawn break, so White has to keep it protected.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops and adds a defender to d4, but the knight is attacked at once by ...dxe4. When it moves, d4 loses a defender and Black wins at least a pawn.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6.strategy: Hits the pawn on d5 at once to open lines against White's centre. If White grabs a second pawn on c6, the d-file opens against d4 and Black's pieces come out with tempo; if White defends with a piece, Black has to make do with development for the pawn.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 Nf6.strategy: Develops with pressure on d5 and offers the pawn for activity, but White simply defends it with a developing move and keeps the extra pawn. Black's compensation is too thin, and the knight blocks the g7 bishop's diagonal.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 Qxd5.strategy: Hangs the queen: the c4 pawn takes it at once, and Black has nothing to recapture with.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6 5.dxc.strategy: Takes a second pawn, and the pawn on c6 eyes b7 and d7. But the d-pawn leaves the d-file: d4 is now attacked by Black's queen and bishop and defended only by White's queen, so Black regains a pawn with an active bishop. White must play accurately to keep the extra material.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6 5.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight and guards d5, so after Black captures there White can retake and stay a pawn up with the pawns on c4 and d4 intact. Black has to find its compensation in quick development and pressure on d4.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6 5.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight and adds a defender to d4, but leaves d5 short of support: after Black takes and the c-pawn recaptures, the pawn is attacked by the queen and defended by nothing, so Black regains the pawn at once.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6 5.dxc.name: Modern Defence: Dunworthy Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d5 4.exd5 c6 5.dxc.strategy: Takes a pawn back at once with the bishop, which is safe on d4: 6.Qxd4 Qxd4 wins the queen for a bishop, because nothing of White's guards d4. White can win the b7 pawn and stay a pawn up, but Black's pieces are active on open lines and the game is balanced.

Recaptures with a developing move that adds a third attacker to d4, but White just plays d5, which hits the knight and keeps the extra pawn with a gain of space. The pressure on d4 is gone and Black has little to show for the pawn.

Recaptures with the b-pawn and opens the b-file, with the queen and bishop still pressing on d4. But White defends it with Nf3 and stays a pawn up, and Black's loosened structure buys activity that does not repay it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3.name: Modern Defence: Averbakh System
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight and guards e4, so the broad pawn centre is solid. White has space and an easy development; Black has to find a way to break the centre with flank pawn moves. Whether the centre proves a strength or a target is the question of the line.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3.strategy: Develops the bishop to a square that backs d4 and prepares to bring the queen to d2 and castle long. White keeps the knight's square open for later; the cost is that the c1 bishop commits before Black has shown its plan.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nf3.strategy: Puts the knight on its natural square before deciding how to support the centre: it covers d4 and e5 and prepares castling. White commits less than with an early bishop move; the cost is that e4 has no support yet, so a black knight on f6 makes White spend a move on it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with a hit on the e4 pawn, which nothing defends yet, so White must spend a move on it. Black gets natural development and prepares to castle, and the pressure on the big centre continues.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nc6.strategy: Adds a second attacker to d4, which the bishop on e3 and the queen defend, and develops the queenside knight. White has to decide between closing the centre with a space-gaining push and keeping d4 supported; either way Black develops with tempo.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 e5.strategy: Strikes at the centre at once: if White takes, the queens come off and Black's king loses castling, though White's pawn centre is dissolved. The break comes early, with the kingside undeveloped, and White can keep a space edge by closing the centre instead.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nf6 5.f3.name: Modern Defence: Averbakh Variation, Pseudo-Sämisch
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nf6 5.f3.strategy: Defends e4 with a pawn, so both knights are free to develop, and prepares to castle long and attack on the kingside. The price is the f3 square for the king's knight; Black must strike at the centre before White is ready.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nf6 5.Nc3.strategy: Defends e4 with a developing move and leaves the f-pawn free, so White can still choose between a solid set-up and a more aggressive one. A knight does the pawn's job on e4, which keeps the centre flexible; the cost is that the knight commits before Black's plan is known.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Be3 Nf6 5.Bd3.strategy: Defends e4 with the bishop, but shuts the queen out of the defence of d4 and exposes the e3 bishop to ...Ng4. Black gains time, and the trade on e3 doubles White's pawns.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 Nc6.name: Modern Defence: Kotov Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 Nc6.strategy: Adds a second attacker to d4, which only the queen defends, and prepares to challenge the centre with the e-pawn. White has to react at once; the choice between closing the centre and defending it shapes the game.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5.strategy: Challenges d4 with a pawn, backed by the g7 bishop. Black wants queenside counterplay and pressure on the long diagonal, but White's centre is already supported and Black is still undeveloped, so the break comes with some risk.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 f5.name: Modern Defence: Randspringer Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 f5.strategy: Strikes at e4 at once, but White takes, and after 5.exf5 gxf5 6.Qh5+ the king must move, losing castling and with the kingside pawns shattered. A speculative idea that makes Black's own king the target.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight with an attack on e4 and prepares to castle. White's broad pawn centre is now a target rather than just an asset: Black keeps every pawn break available and has to prove the centre overextended, while White has to show it can support and use it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Be3.strategy: Adds a second guard to d4, so a capture on d4 can be met by recapturing with the bishop and White keeps the centre. The bishop also eyes the queenside and the c5 pawn, at the cost of allowing a queen sortie that pins the knight.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Nge2.strategy: Keeps the f-pawn and the c1 bishop free, supports d4 from the side and guards c3, so a pin on that knight is less dangerous. The knight is modestly placed, and White's centre stays flexible.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.dxc5.strategy: Wins a pawn for the moment but gives up the centre: the d4 pawn that closed the g7 bishop's diagonal is gone. Black can win the pawn back at once with a pin on the c3 knight.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Be3.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Anhanguera
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Be3.strategy: Pins the c3 knight to the king and prepares to put it under pressure once a capture on d4 opens the bishop's diagonal. The queen leaves the centre early, and White can unpin with a developing move.

Adds a third attacker to d4, which the bishop and the queen defend only twice, so White must defend it again or resolve the tension at once. Closing the centre with a pawn push gives White more space, but Black's knight gets a good square on d4, and Black keeps castling and the long diagonal.

Natural development with a hit on e4, but it needs care: after White takes on c5, recapturing with the d-pawn allows the queen trade with check and then Bxc5, which wins a pawn. Black must find a more exact answer, so the move is playable but less accurate than adding pressure on d4 first.

Takes on d4 with a pawn that attacks both the e3 bishop and the c3 knight, so White has to recapture at once with the bishop. The c-file opens for Black, and the bishop on d4 becomes a target for Black's knights.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.dxc5.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Quetzalcoatlus Gambit
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.dxc5.strategy: Pins the knight and hits c5, but White simply plays cxd6: after ...exd6 and Bd2 White is a clean pawn up and the pin is gone. Black has lost a pawn for nothing.

Recaptures the pawn at once, so the material is level and Black's structure is healthy. White can trade queens with check, which leaves Black's king in the middle without the right to castle, but Black's pieces are active and the position stays close to level.
Develops and attacks e4 but leaves the c5 pawn alone: White simply takes again with cxd6 and keeps an extra pawn, while Black has only its development to show for it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Nge2.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Bogolubovia
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4 d6 4.Nc3 c5 5.Nge2.strategy: Pins the c3 knight against the king and ties White's pieces up in the centre. Black gets active play for an early queen move; c3 is guarded twice, so nothing is lost at once.

Resolves the tension at once: White recaptures on d4 and the g7 bishop immediately eyes the recapturing piece. White keeps a broad centre with pawns on c4 and e4, but Black develops freely and can trade pieces to ease the cramp.

Develops a piece, hits the e4 pawn and keeps the tension on d4 for later. If White closes the centre with a pawn on d5, Black gets a flexible position with play on the queenside; if White takes on c5, the queens come off or Black recovers the pawn.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6.name: Modern Defence
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6.strategy: Solid and flexible: the pawn covers e5 and c5 and Black waits to see how White sets up the centre. Black keeps the choice of central breaks for later, with a compact structure.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5.strategy: Hits d4 at once, before White has built the centre with e4. The pawn is backed by the bishop on g7, and Black asks White to commit. It leads to sharp play with early queen sorties.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight and eyes e4 and d5, the most flexible reply to White's build-up. Black can keep the kingside fianchetto and castle, or strike at the centre, depending on how White sets up the pawns.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5.strategy: Takes space and closes the centre. It opens the long diagonal for the g7 bishop, which now bears on the c3 knight, so White accepts the risk of doubled pawns for a protected space advantage and, if Black takes, the two bishops.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.e3.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Queen Pterodactyl, Quiet Line
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.e3.strategy: Defends d4 with a pawn and prepares quiet development, keeping the centre as it is. It shuts in the c1 bishop for the time being and does not try for a space advantage, so Black reaches a comfortable game.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight toward castling and guards d4, so that taking on d4 only brings the knight into the centre. White keeps a firm grip on the centre and the d5 and b5 squares, while Black looks for counterplay on the queenside.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.dxc5.strategy: Wins a pawn for the moment and gives up the d4 pawn that held the centre. Black strikes back with the queen on a5, pinning the c3 knight and hitting c5, so White has to give the pawn back or accept a damaged structure.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6.strategy: The solid reply: defends c5 and shores up the centre. White has more space, but the g7 bishop keeps its open diagonal and Black's queenside pawn play gives counterplay. Black also keeps the bishop rather than trading it for the knight.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+.strategy: Trades the fianchettoed bishop for the knight to double White's pawns. The c-pawns become targets, but White gets the two bishops and a space advantage, so Black has to attack the weak pawns before they are consolidated.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Qa5.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Fianchetto, Queen Benoni Pterodactyl
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Qa5.strategy: Pins the c3 knight and, with the bishop, attacks it twice, but Bd2 guards it again and breaks the pin. The queen has gained little for its early sortie, and White keeps the space advantage on d5.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.b.strategy: The only recapture: White accepts doubled c-pawns for the two bishops and a space advantage. The c3 and c4 pawns are targets, so White needs active piece play and quick development to keep Black from attacking them.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.B.strategy: Leaves the knight lost: Black takes the bishop with check, and after the recapture is a whole piece up for nothing.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.Q.strategy: Loses the queen on top of the knight: Black takes it with check and gives up only a bishop for it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.b.name: Modern Defence: Beefeater Variation
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.b.strategy: Stops e4 outright, since a pawn there would simply be taken, and claims the e4 square for a knight. Black keeps White's broad centre from forming and takes space on the kingside, at the cost of loosening it.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.b.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Fianchetto, Queen Pteranodon
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 Bxc3+ 5.b.strategy: Attacks the undefended c3 pawn, but White can leave it: capturing on c3 lets Bd2 hit the queen, which has to run while White is ahead in development. The queen has stepped out early and White's centre grows unhindered.
Develops and eyes e4, but cannot stop White from taking the broad centre with e4. White's two bishops and space then give the more comfortable game, and Black has to go after the doubled c-pawns.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4.strategy: Builds the full pawn centre with c4, d5 and e4, giving White a big space advantage. Black cannot easily drive the pawns back and must undermine them with the g7 bishop and flank pawn breaks, while White must keep the c3 knight supported.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.Nf3.strategy: Develops the knight toward castling and guards the centre without committing the e-pawn. Black can still take on c3 and double White's pawns, but White then gets the bishop pair and quick development in return.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.Bd2.strategy: Guards the c3 knight so that a trade on c3 can be answered by a recapture with the bishop, which keeps White's pawns intact and puts the bishop on the long diagonal. It is a slow, defensive move that gives Black time to develop.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 Q.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Benoni Quetzalcoatlus
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 Q.strategy: Pins the c3 knight and attacks it twice with the bishop, but Bd2 guards it again and breaks the pin. The queen has spent a move for little, and White keeps the space and develops freely.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 B.strategy: Removes the knight at the price of the fianchettoed bishop. White's c-pawns are doubled but a big centre and the two bishops are the compensation; Black must go after the weak pawns.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 N.strategy: The natural developing move: Black attacks the e4 pawn and prepares to castle, leaving the bishop on g7 to work against the centre. Black accepts less space and answers it with piece pressure on e4 and pawn breaks on the queenside.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 B.strategy: The only recapture: the doubled c-pawns buy the bishop pair and a massive centre. White must use them actively, since the pawns on c3 and c4 are a target.
Leaves the knight lost: Black takes the bishop with check, and after the recapture is a whole piece up for nothing.
Walks the king into the centre instead of recapturing: Black simply retreats the bishop, stays a piece up and leaves White's king stranded.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 B.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Central, Benoni Beefeater Pterodactyl
1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5 4.d5 d6 5.e4 B.strategy: Attacks the c3 pawn with the idea of taking it with check, but Bd2 guards it and develops a piece. The queen has gained little, while White keeps the big centre and the bishop pair.
Develops a piece and attacks the e4 pawn, which nothing guards, so White must spend a move defending it. Black keeps the queen sortie in reserve and meets the doubled pawns with calm development.

Heads for b6 to attack the c4 pawn, the target of the doubled structure, but the route is slow and the knight blocks the c8 bishop. White gets time to consolidate the centre and keeps the better game.
Answers the big centre by fixing it with the e-pawn. White's bishop pair has few open lines, the doubled c-pawns stay weak, and Black gets a sound, closed structure.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 4.e4.strategy: Builds the big centre with c4, d4 and e4 now that the knight guards it. White has space, Black the solid position and flank breaks to strike with, so the game is shaped by whether the centre holds.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 4.Nf3.strategy: Develops the king's knight and guards the centre without committing the e-pawn. It keeps White's options open between a big pawn centre and a quieter set-up, while Black gets comfortable development and castles.

1.c4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6 4.g3.strategy: Fianchettoes the bishop to mirror Black's, aiming it along the long diagonal. It gives up the ambition of a big pawn centre for a solid game, so Black can castle and break in the centre without trouble.
